etymologies.etymologyHTML: Old French tornoiement (Modern French tournoiement) from the verb tornoier.

definitions.definition: (historical) During the Middle Ages, a series of battles and other contests designed to prepare knights for war.
A series of games; either the same game played many times, or a succession of games related by a single theme; played competitively to determine a single winning team or individual.

quote.text: England secured their place at Euro 2012 with a scrambled draw in Montenegro - but Wayne Rooney was sent off and will miss the start of the tournament.

definitions.definition: (graph theory) A digraph obtained by assigning a direction to each edge in an undirected complete graph.
